instructions.text: Read the entire method first and measure the following ingredients before turning on the heat: 1 3/4 cups Flour; 1 cup + 2 1/2 Tbsp Butter, divided; Up to 1/3 cup Water, chilled; 1/2 cup Onion, finely chopped; 14 ounces Smoked Salmon, chopped; 2 tsp Fresh Chives, chopped; 1 clove Garlic, chopped; 2 tsp Fresh Basil, chopped; 5 whole Eggs; 1 cup Milk; 1 cup Whipping Cream. Keep ingredients marked optional separate until their step.

Prepare these ingredients before cooking: Onion: finely chopped; Smoked Salmon: chopped; Chives: Fresh; chopped; Garlic: chopped; Basil: Fresh; chopped. Wash produce under running water before cutting. Use a cutting board and a sharp knife; keep raw meat and its utensils separate from ready-to-eat ingredients.
Combine all pastry ingredients in a food processor (mix flour and butter, then add water gradually while mixing).
Gather into a ball, cover with plastic wrap and chill 1 hour.

Saute onion until shiny in the butter. Stir frequently so the ingredients soften evenly without sticking or burning; reduce the heat if they darken too quickly. For this stovetop step, start over medium heat and lower it if the food browns before the center cooks.
Stir in salmon, chives, garlic, and basil.
Roll out the dough to fit a 10" tart pan.
Arrange the salmon mixture in the pre-baked tart shell.
Whisk eggs with milk and cream, season with pepper and pour in the tart shell.
Bake about 30 minutes at 325F, until puffed and golden.

Before serving, check the center of the cooked egg mixture with a food thermometer: it must reach 160°F (71°C), with no runny raw egg. For a casserole containing reheated cooked meat, use 165°F (74°C). Continue cooking if needed.

Turn off any burners or oven when cooking is finished. Follow the cooling or resting instruction above before cutting or serving. Serve the finished dish as directed; allow hot portions to cool enough to eat.

source.author: Joel Maxuel
source.originalInstructions:
1. Combine all pastry ingredients in a food processor (mix flour and butter, then add water gradually while mixing).
2. Gather into a ball, cover with plastic wrap and chill 1 hour.
3. Saute onion until shiny in the butter.
4. Stir in salmon, chives, garlic, and basil. Cool.
5. Preheat the oven to 400F.
6. Roll out the dough to fit a 10" tart pan. Prick with a fork.
7. Arrange the salmon mixture in the pre-baked tart shell.
8. Whisk eggs with milk and cream, season with pepper and pour in the tart shell.
9. Bake about 30 minutes at 325F, until puffed and golden.
